purpose: Normalize current frontier-model capability evidence into real effect classes for obsolescence. This is not an implementation checklist.

normalized_effect_classes.real_effect: Produce objectively exact mathematical/computational results when a formal solver or deterministic algorithm can define ground truth.
Solve difficult unfamiliar math/science/technical problems where the path is not already reducible to one known deterministic operator.
Diagnose and change unfamiliar software systems end-to-end, including root cause, implementation, tests, and regression control.
Turn an underspecified question into current, source-grounded, decision-useful conclusions with provenance and contradiction handling.
Recognize a missing capability, discover candidate tools, learn their contracts, choose the best route, and use it correctly.
Coordinate dependent tools/subtasks across long horizons while preserving state, scope, and causal ordering.
Perceive and act through rendered interfaces and arbitrary applications when structured APIs are insufficient.
Extract, relate, and reason over dense screenshots, documents, charts, diagrams, and mixed visual/text artifacts.
Recover the right facts/state from very large histories or stores and apply them correctly without losing causal context.
Continue consequential work for long periods across interruption/failure while preserving identity, goals, evidence, and progress.
Interpret underspecified goals, stay within scope, notice material ambiguity, and request human input only when necessary.
Detect likely errors, construct independent checks, falsify hypotheses, and verify actual external outcomes.
Produce correct, usable spreadsheets, documents, presentations, analyses, and workflow outputs under professional constraints.
Infer structure and solve unfamiliar tasks where no known domain procedure or direct tool mapping is given.

anti_claim: Presence in this surface means the behavior is a frontier-obsolescence target. It does not imply that Project Brain lacks it completely or that a named frontier model uniquely owns it.
